title: The affine Bernstein theorem in dimensions three through nine
main_claim: For 3≤n≤9, a smooth locally uniformly convex affine maximal graph whose graph is complete in the induced Euclidean metric is an elliptic paraboloid. Via TW2002, the same holds for affine-complete affine maximal hypersurfaces. The proof shows that the maximal number of directions of convex-limit models is k=1, using a logarithmic Poincaré inequality on tubes against polynomial bounds on log cells. This gives uniform balance of sections and a modulus of strict convexity, which then feed into the Trudinger–Wang interior estimates and rescaling.

issues.description: The interior estimate is quoted from Trudinger–Wang in a repackaged form: a prescribed section modulus on O = B_{1/4}, with sections taken inside O, gives lower Hessian and C^q bounds on O'. The paper does not show that TW's hypotheses (for example, sections compactly contained in the domain, or a domain that is itself a section) match this repackaging. The final rescaling step depends on it.
issues.evidence: The paper states only 'This is [TW2000, Theorem 4.2], stated in terms of a prescribed lower bound for the modulus of convexity.' I could not check this against the source. Everything up to producing the modulus (Lemma normalized-modulus) checks out.

issues.description: Not an error, only an observation. The quadratic form λ(n+1-2λ)-(n+2)^2/16 is also positive for n=2 with λ∈(1/2,1). For n=10 it fails only when k=2. So the dimension restriction comes entirely from the k=2 case, which matches the paper's remark. No issue with correctness.
issues.evidence: At n=2 the form is -(2λ-1)(λ-1), which is positive on (1/2,1). At n=10 it is -(2λ-9)(λ-1), which needs λ>1, but λ<k/2 forces k≥3.

coverage: I read all five sections in full and rederived these by hand: the tube affine-area density and invariant measure; the Euler equation in support coordinates and its log form; the f-equation (eq. tube-f-equation); the integration-by-parts drifts; the p- and d-identities and their exact cancellation; the coercivity determinant (-8n^2+88n-137)/128 ≥ 7/128 with k-2λ ≥ 1/8; the log-inequality chain rule; the cap identity, both the ψ and ψ' coefficients; the Σa a^T identity; the Hölder exponents θ=1/(2(1-δ)) and I_0 = μ_0^{2δ} h^{nδ}(det R)^{1-2δ}; the positive-cap-area concavity comparison; the strip area scaling ε^{nδ}; the centering contradiction and (k+1)-model construction, including the interpolation weight a = 1/(2-q) and the |z| ≤ 4dT bound; and the doubling constants β and A. I also checked the rescaling D^3u = O(t^{-1/2}). I did not check the cited TW2000 and TW2002 theorems against their sources.
